Hi Jared / team,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion and appreciate the clarity on your key goals. Per our notes, I wanted to capture the proposed POC evaluation plan so everyone has a single reference:

Summary (proposal)
- Objective: validate Redwood inference for multi-user search-ranking flows and cost/latency under representative traffic.
- Timeline: 4-week POC (Week 0: setup & baseline; Weeks 1-3: eval runs + tuning).
- Success criteria (pass/fail):
  - Latency: median request latency <= 150ms at 95%ile with 1.5x expected QPS
  - Quality: top-5 ranking MRR improvement >= 7% vs baseline OR no regression vs current model for 95% of benchmark queries
  - Cost: estimated per-query cost <= $0.010 after batching/caching optimizations
- Ownership: Acme provides test dataset and baseline metrics; Redwood delivers evaluation harness, infra, and weekly checkpoints.
- Evaluation methodology option A/B (need alignment):
  A) Offline evals — run labeled test sets with grading rubric (MRR, precision@k, per-intent buckets)
  B) Online shadow/parallel runs — run Redwood in shadow mode on a subset of live traffic to measure live latency and end-to-end ranking differences

Next steps
1) Confirm which evaluation methodology you prefer (A or B) — both recommended; we can run offline first and shadow in week 2.
2) Share dataset and baseline by EOD Tuesday (6/15).
3) Kickoff meeting to schedule setup (propose 6/17 10am PT).

Attaching a first-pass eval plan + standard POC terms for procurement to review.

Thanks —
Dylan

Dylan / Rachel —

Quick draft rubric and recommended ownership below. Happy to turn into a one-pager for Acme.

Recommended owners
- Evaluation harness & infra: Marissa Cole (primary), Rachel Kim (backup)
- Weekly checkpoints & stakeholder updates: Marissa (leads), Dylan (customer-facing SE)

Grading rubric (example — weights can be tuned by intent)
- Primary metric (weight 60%): MRR@5 across entire test corpus
- Secondary metric (weight 25%): Precision@1 (to capture top-hit relevance)
- Behavioral/robustness (weight 10%): Intent-level pass rate (percent of intents with >= baseline quality)
- Operational (weight 5%): Median latency at 95th percentile (operational guardrail; fail if > 200ms)

Score calculation (simple example)
- Normalize each metric relative to baseline (baseline = 0). For uplift metrics, score = (model_metric - baseline_metric)/baseline_metric. For latency (lower-is-better), we convert to a penalty where any value over the latency threshold reduces the final score proportionally. Final score = 0.6*MRR_score + 0.25*P@1_score + 0.10*intent_pass_rate - 0.05*latency_penalty. Pass threshold = 0.07 (7% overall uplift equivalent).

Offline vs Online guidance
- Start with offline evals (fast, reproducible) to tune model variants and ensure no regression across intents.
- If offline uplift >= 4% and no intent regressions, run a 1-week online shadow on 10% traffic to validate latencies and real-world ranking differences.

Deliverables for Week 0/1
- Week 0: infra setup, data ingest, baseline run (Marissa)
- Week 1: offline eval report + grading rubric scored (Rachel)
- Week 2: optional shadow run + live metrics (Marissa + Dylan)

I'll produce a one-page rubric + scoring spreadsheet and attach.
